title: The leak scan passes a key block whose lines carry a /// or //! comment prefix
goal: kbcommon.leak_hits flags an EC or PGP key block whose armor and body lines each carry a /// or //! prefix, as it flags one behind //

run: import base64,os,sys;sys.path.insert(0,'_tools');import kbcommon;d='-'*5;b=base64.b64encode(os.urandom(96)).decode();hit=lambda t:any(k=='secret' for k,_ in kbcommon.leak_hits(t));m=[p for p in ('/// ','//! ') if not hit(p+d+'BEGIN EC PRIVATE KEY'+d+chr(10)+p+b[:64]+chr(10)+p+b[64:])];print('prefixes passing:',m);sys.exit(1 if m else 0)

notes: Found 2026-10-23 by the SP-evq2flqc fresh review: the gap takes // as a pair, so a third / or ! leaves no 20-character base64 run after the label. A table whose delimiter row sits between the label row and the key row also passes (- is no gap character); that case is outside the goal.
